# StockMem: An Event-Reflection Memory Framework for Stock Forecasting

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Predicting next-day stock price movement direction (up/down) from noisy online financial news using an LLM with a domain-specific event-reflection memory. | “You are a stock analyst specializing in {stock}. You need to predict tomorrow’s stock price movement (up/down) based on the following analytical elements.” |
| **architecture** | Dual-layer memory: Event Memory (LLM event extraction into 57 types, daily merging via vector clustering plus LLM, event tracking for incremental info) and Reflection Memory (LLM causal explanations with true labels); retrieval via Jaccard event-sequence similarity plus LLM filtering; LLM prediction. | “The final prediction is generated by LLM_{predict} through synthesizing the following three types of information:” |
| **data** | Daily online financial news from CSMAR China Stock Market Research Database; four Chinese technology stocks (iFlytek, Industrial Fulian, Cambricon, Hygon); daily returns with ±1% threshold, flat days excluded. | “We conducted experiments on four technology companies: iFlytek, Industrial Fulian, Cambricon, and Hygon. Daily returns were used to measure price movements, with a ±1% threshold applied to classify directions due to the sector’s high volatility.” |
| **window** | Trained on Q1 2024 (January 1 to March 31), tested on Q2 2024 (April 1 to June 30), with online incremental memory updates after each test prediction. | “the model was trained on data from the first quarter of 2024 (January 1 to March 31) and tested on data from the second quarter (April 1 to June 30).” |
| **models** | DeepSeek-V3 as core LLM; BGE-M3 for text vectorization. | “We employs DeepSeek-V3(Liu et al., 2024) as the core language model, while text vectorization utilizes the BGE-M3(Chen et al., 2024) model.” |
| **baselines** | Memory-augmented models FinMem, MemP, MemGPT, and Zep (paper says five but lists four). | “To comprehensively evaluate the performance of the proposed framework, we selected five representative memory-augmented models as baselines:” |
| **headline_result** | On iFlytek, StockMem reaches ACC 0.6253 and MCC 0.1692 (Q2 2024 test); other stocks: Industrial Fulian 0.5714/0.1277, Cambricon 0.5622/0.1363, Hygon 0.5403/0.1186.
